title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for parallel/multi-tool calls with retries and result injection
author: Ariana Chen
description:
Motivation: Improve ergonomics and reliability for tool/function-calling when callers request multiple tools in parallel or when tools are retried and their outputs must be injected back into the model context. Current behavior had races, inconsistent injection ordering, and streaming interruptions when parallel tool results arrived at different times. This caused customer-visible regressions for compositional workflows (assistant calling multiple agents) and brittle retry semantics.

Summary: This change implements a deterministic orchestration layer for multi-tool and parallel tool execution. Key user-visible behaviors: (1) parallel tool calls can be requested via the new `parallel_tools` flag on tool_call requests; results are injected atomically per-call according to a user-configurable merge strategy (append|replace|named-insert); (2) each tool invocation gets a stable `tool_call_id` opaque string which is present in model tokens and streaming events so downstream consumers can correlate partial outputs and retries; (3) retries use idempotent execution tokens and backoff policy while preserving injection ordering and deduping results; (4) streaming remains stable: partial tool outputs are forwarded immediately with metadata, but final injection into the model context happens only when the orchestration group reaches quiescence or when the merge strategy dictates.

Design details: The runtime now stages tool invocations into a ToolExecutionGroup (TEG) per top-level tool call request. A TEG tracks member tool_call_ids, expected responses, retry state, and the configured merge_strategy. The executor exposes three new surface signals in the OpenAI-compatible streaming wire format: `tool_call_started`, `tool_call_partial`, and `tool_call_completed` (each includes tool_call_id and sequence_index). To maintain compatibility with existing integrations we preserve the previous `tool_result_inject` behavior by default, but when `parallel_tools=true` we switch to grouped atomic injections.

Backward compatibility & migration: Default behavior is unchanged unless callers opt in to `parallel_tools` or new merge strategies. Existing clients that rely on the previous streaming semantics will continue to work. The OpenAI compatibility layer maps the new streaming events to legacy events when applicable and adds the `tool_call_id` as `metadata.tool_call_id` in the legacy event envelope.

Testing & rollout: Unit tests for TEG lifecycle, concurrency, and deduping added. Integration tests simulate interleaved responses, partial streaming, and retry storms. E2E canary deployed to staging and Canary cluster with 48-hour soak. CI initially failed lint/tests due to a race in the retry backoff; fix included in second commit. Rollout plan: gradual traffic ramp with feature flag `tool_call.parallel_execution` starting at 0.5% -> 100% across hosted API and Dedicated.

Alternatives considered: (a) synchronous blocking execution for multi-tool calls (rejected — would hurt latency); (b) enqueueing tool responses into the model token stream without grouping (rejected — causes nondeterminism on retries).

Checklist: implemented feature + tests, updated API docs (OpenAPI snippets), added observability metrics (teg.size, teg.latency, tool_call.retry_count), added migration notes in redwood-docs.

References: ENG-8112 design doc (internal), several incident notes (support SUP-3942) and prior PRs for tool-calling ergonomics (see pr-41234, pr-42790).
